name: Sebadoh
label: Sub Pop
lede: Thrown out of Dinosaur Jr., Lou Barlow turned his home cassettes into a band with Eric Gaffney and Jason Loewenstein. Three songwriters, one four-track, then a major label that gave them five weeks in Los Angeles and dropped them within weeks of the record.

eras.title: The songs Dinosaur Jr. didn't need
eras.text: While J Mascis took over Dinosaur Jr., bassist Lou Barlow filled cassettes at home in western Massachusetts. With Eric Gaffney he made that a band, and when Dinosaur Jr. fired him, Sebadoh became his main one.

years.cap: Dinosaur Jr. with Barlow on bass, Toronto
years.h: Bassist Lou Barlow starts Sebadoh in Northampton, Massachusetts
years.p: Dinosaur Jr. is [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]]'s band, so [[Lou Barlow|6523f86d-11d3-489e-81f6-6cbe08c367de]] gives his songs to a duo with [[Eric Gaffney|820d149f-836a-4527-a2ab-14fb079bc212]].

years.h: Weed Forestin' is a cassette, and the band name is a mumble
years.p: The first tape with the name on it. Barlow kept muttering a nonsense word on his home recordings, and it stuck.

years.h: Dinosaur Jr. throws Barlow out after Bug
years.p: Years of friction with Mascis end with the bassist fired. Sebadoh goes from side project to his main band.

years.h: Homestead's Gerard Cosloy puts the home tapes out on LP
years.p: The Freed Man gives [[Gerard Cosloy|b3c600d5-e1dd-4525-855d-6d4f950c3be6]]'s label a full album of home recordings, Barlow and Gaffney songs side by side.

years.h: Jason Loewenstein joins, and Sebadoh becomes a trio
years.p: [[Jason Loewenstein|d06bfcfa-7be5-40ca-82be-4c7d3bdb44c3]] arrives in the summer. Across 1989 and 1990 the band plays only about ten shows, in western Massachusetts, Boston and New York.

eras.title: Cheap tapes, three songwriters
eras.text: Barlow wrote bruised folk, Gaffney drones and hardcore bursts, Loewenstein something in between. The records cost little, and people started calling the sound lo-fi.

yt: Full show, Middle East, Cambridge, December 1990
years.h: "Gimme Indie Rock" sends up the scene it belongs to
years.p: The first Sebadoh single with Loewenstein, on Homestead, becomes one of that scene's anthems.

years.h: Sebadoh III cost $1,300 to make
years.p: Cut in late March 1991 at Fort Apache in Boston and at home. Spin ranked it No. 41 of the '90s, and it sits beside Pavement's Slanted and Enchanted as a lo-fi cornerstone.

years.h: "The Freed Pig" is Barlow's letter to Mascis
years.p: The opening track of Sebadoh III answers Barlow's firing from Dinosaur Jr. [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]] cover it in 1994.

years.h: A tour with Mike Watt's fIREHOSE ends in a Sub Pop contract
years.p: After the road with [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]]'s [[fIREHOSE|33e09dd8-a998-4e1a-9e69-1a6567a3803d]], Sebadoh signs to Sub Pop in the US, Domino in the UK and City Slang in Germany.

years.h: Two EPs, two months apart, become one American album
years.p: Sub Pop folds Rocking the Forest and Sebadoh vs. Helmet into Smash Your Head on the Punk Rock.
years.xp: Gaffney quit and came back three times between 1990 and 1993. His fill-in, Boston record-store clerk [[Bob Fay|87509777-a7ba-4a80-aa83-42dc8819236e]], plays on half of Rocking the Forest and on two tracks of Sebadoh vs. Helmet.

eras.title: Gaffney walks, Bakesale lands
eras.text: Sebadoh moved into real studios and Gaffney moved out. With Bob Fay on drums and Loewenstein writing as an equal, the band made the record fans love most.

years.h: Bob Weston engineers the first all-studio Sebadoh album
years.p: Bubble & Scrape is the last with Gaffney songs. Barlow sings a duet with Seana Carmody of [[Swirlies|4ec4a033-ba44-41ca-8e09-3bf94fc08523]].

years.cap: Barlow, Loewenstein and Fay, Toronto, September 1994
years.h: Gaffney leaves with a list of demands, mid-Bakesale
years.p: He wanted a third of the advance, his own sessions and no touring. Barlow said no, and Bob Fay took over the drums.
years.xp:
Barlow told Under the Radar that Gaffney had already bailed on Sebadoh's first tour opening for [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], a week out, with a long letter listing what Barlow was doing wrong. Gaffney's own version: he wanted a band where he was the songwriter and guitarist.

Barlow's verdict on the aftermath: "When he left, it felt like we could just have fun." Loewenstein, who had written one or two songs a record, now had to bring an equal number.

years.h: The Bakesale cover is Barlow at age one, shot by his mother
years.p: Bob Fay and his brothers are on the back. The album reaches No. 40 in the UK and No. 16 on Spin's best of 1994.

years.h: Barlow's side band, the Folk Implosion, goes Top 40 with Natural One
years.p: [[The Folk Implosion|31722656-e14d-4f3f-8ecb-27cba9ce3a15]], his duo with John Davis, lands the song on the Kids soundtrack.

eras.title: Fire your drummer
eras.text: Sub Pop spent money, Sebadoh charted, Fay was fired and Sire signed the band. Then came an expensive record in Los Angeles while Barlow's life came apart, and a stop.

years.h: A Harmacy producer tells Barlow to fire his drummer
years.p: Sub Pop spends big on the album, and Barlow recalls the pressure starting right away over Bob Fay's drumming. Fay plays on Harmacy anyway, his last Sebadoh album.

years.h: The Harmacy cover is a pharmacy in Cashel, Ireland, missing its P
years.p: Loewenstein shot it on tour. Sebadoh's first charting US album reaches No. 126, with Ocean at No. 23 on Modern Rock.

years.h: Louisville's Russ Pollard takes the drums after Bob Fay is fired
years.p: Loewenstein brings in his friend [[Russ Pollard|986b1847-ebee-47e5-92a6-cdd864f3b287]], who can also switch instruments. Sebadoh signs to Sire while still owing Sub Pop.
years.xp: Vice reports that Sire president Seymour Stein called the band "kings of grunge" at the signing dinner. The major-label advances for Sebadoh on Sire and the Folk Implosion on Interscope helped pay for Barlow's house in Silver Lake.

years.h: Five weeks at Chick Corea's Los Angeles studio
years.p: Sebadoh makes The Sebadoh at Mad Hatter. Loewenstein remembers the luxury of time: "We had so much time."
years.xp: Barlow told Vice it was his worst year: he had found out his wife was having an affair and was using speed during the sessions. He says he was trying not to fall apart between vocal takes on Tree.

years.h: Sire drops Sebadoh weeks after The Sebadoh peaks at No. 197
years.p: Flame reaches No. 30 in the UK, but the album sells about a quarter of Harmacy's first-year total.

years.h: On tour with Modest Mouse, Dallas shrinks to a roomful
years.p: A year earlier, Barlow told Vice, the band had drawn 400 or 500 there. Support slot: [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]].

years.h: Sebadoh stops, and Barlow and Loewenstein barely talk
years.p: Barlow turns to the Folk Implosion and Loewenstein to his solo album At Sixes and Sevens. Barlow says he just gave up.
years.xp: The two or three years of near silence ended with Domino's anniversary invitation. The Sebadoh stays the band's last studio album for more than a decade, until Defend Yourself in 2013.

eras.title: Domino's party, then the classic three
eras.text: A record label's birthday brought the band back as a duo. Four years later the original trio, Gaffney included, toured for the first time in fourteen years.

years.h: Domino's 10th birthday brings Barlow and Loewenstein back as a duo
years.p: Domino Records asks Sebadoh to play the party. The two reform and play shows into early 2004.

years.h: The original Dinosaur Jr. reunites on The Late Late Show
years.p: Barlow is back with Mascis, on The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson.

years.cap: Barlow, Loewenstein and Gaffney on the 2007 reunion tour
years.h: The Sebadoh III trio tours again after 14 years
years.p: Billed as Sebadoh Classic, Barlow, Gaffney and Loewenstein hit the road as Domino starts reissuing the early albums.

years.h: Bubble & Scrape front to back at Koko, London
years.p: Sebadoh plays the whole album for All Tomorrow's Parties' Don't Look Back series.

eras.title: Post-drama
eras.text: With Bob D'Amico on drums, Sebadoh became a working band again: reissues, two albums on indie labels, no chaos. Barlow's word for it is post-drama.

years.h: Bob D'Amico takes the drum stool from Gaffney
years.p: [[Bob D'Amico|7d469750-76ea-43ea-aa43-c0566c5fa4d2]], Loewenstein's bandmate in [[The Fiery Furnaces|2c916f95-f6ba-46fa-b9d8-dc0d9379f603]] and Circle of Buzzards, joins for a tour behind the Bakesale deluxe reissue.

years.h: Jeff Mangum asks Sebadoh to his All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]]'s [[Jeff Mangum|6a7b9d5e-a863-4a90-a056-77942e9f43de]] curates the Minehead festival, the same month Weed Forestin' is reissued.

years.h: Defend Yourself ends a 14-year wait for a Sebadoh album
years.p: Out on Joyful Noise, it debuts at No. 1 on a Billboard chart for new alternative artists, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Barlow, Loewenstein and D'Amico, Fox Theatre, Vancouver, June 2019
years.h: Act Surprised lands on Dangerbird with no drama
years.p: Sebadoh's ninth album, made with D'Amico. Barlow says the band is past the fighting.

years.h: Harmacy turns 30 with a Sub Pop expanded edition
years.p: Due on double LP and CD with 16 bonus tracks: alternate versions, B-sides, BBC sessions and live cuts.

sources.title: Under the Radar: Lou Barlow on the 20th Anniversary of Bakesale
